intro.title: Discover Kupittaa Park
intro.description:
Step into Kupittaa Park and you are embraced by serene Nordic greenery — open lawns, mature trees, a calm lake and winding paths, with no commercial bustle.

At about 24 hectares, the park is Turku's largest continuous green space. Highlights include the bird pond, the Kupittaanlahte playground and traffic park for children, the Adventure Park (Seikkailupuisto), a multi-sport court, and Finland's oldest outdoor swimming pool, built in 1912.

Visitors move at an unhurried pace — joggers on the paths, picnickers on the lawns, children playing. A century-old spring pavilion, vintage sculptures and plaques add cultural depth. There is no rushing here, only slowing down and finding peace.

sections.title: Kupittaa Park Through the Years
sections.content:
Kupittaa Park's origins trace back to the 1820s, when a promenade was laid out beside a spa spring. Across the 19th and 20th centuries it was formalised into a public urban park — today described by the City of Turku as Finland's oldest urban park.

The park's sacred spring carries a legend: it is said that in 1155 Bishop Henry baptised Finland's first Christians here. For centuries this was a spa and gathering place, holding both religious and secular memory.

Since then the park has expanded repeatedly, adding the outdoor pool (1912), children's playgrounds and sports facilities, growing into a green core that blends nature, history and recreation.

sections.title: Gardens & Landscape
sections.content:
Spanning approximately 24 hectares, the park features expansive lawns, formal gardens, winding paths and lake scenery as its core, complemented by a historic spring pavilion, vintage sculptures, commemorative plaques and century-old trees.

Home to Finland's oldest outdoor swimming pool (built 1912), the Kupittaanlahte playground and the Adventure Park (Seikkailupuisto) — natural landscapes and recreational facilities blend together. The layout balances open, natural greenery with structured garden design.

sections.title: Cultural Significance
sections.content:
Turku's urban green lung and the core gathering place for locals across generations, witnessing Finland's transformation from medieval times to the modern era.

The sacred spring carries the legend of Finland's 1155 baptism, a spiritual symbol of Finnish national culture and of the Nordic outdoor lifestyle. For centuries, Kupittaa Park has witnessed Turku's evolution from a medieval town to a modern city — from an exclusive spa ground to shared public space — and remains an irreplaceable retreat for locals.

sections.title: Outdoor Swimming Pool
sections.content:
Finland's oldest outdoor swimming pool, built in 1912, remains the most popular summer facility. In 2026 the season ran from 5 June to 13 September and has now ended; the next season's dates are published by the City of Turku.

Admission is charged and is set by the city — current prices are listed on turku.fi/kupittaan-maauimala. The pool sits beside the park, so swimmers can enjoy the green surroundings.

transport.title: How to Get Here
transport.fromAirportDesc: Take the airport bus to Turku city centre, then continue by Föli bus to Kupittaa (about 25–30 minutes total). A taxi is the simplest option for groups or luggage.
transport.fromStationDesc: Take a Föli bus from Turku Central Station; several routes stop near the park, about a 10-minute ride plus a short walk. Buses run frequently.
transport.fromOldTownDesc: Kupittaa is within walking distance of Turku's Old Town and the Aura River waterfront via well-connected pedestrian paths — ideal for a combined walking tour.
transport.cyclingDesc: Public cycling stations are available around the park, suitable for short trips. Park paths are gentle and comfortable for cycling.
transport.dayPassDesc: Purchase a Turku public transport day pass for unlimited Föli bus rides, efficiently explore all city attractions.

route.title: Recommended Route
route.overview: Recommended to enter the park in the early morning. Start from the main entrance, stroll along the central tree-lined path, visit the sacred spring, century-old trees and the spring pavilion, wander through the gardens and lakeside, tour the children's playground and outdoor pool, finally relax on the lawn area. The entire route is relaxed — approximately 2 hours for pure sightseeing, half a day for a deeper exploration.

Stroll along the central tree-lined path, admire expansive lawns and lush tree landscapes

Wander through garden paths, admire seasonal planting and horticultural designs
Stroll along the lakeside, observe waterbirds and lake scenery up close
Tour the children's playground and Adventure Park, experience the family recreation atmosphere
Visit the outdoor swimming pool area, learn about Finland's oldest pool's history
Relax at the expansive lawn area, experience locals' daily picnic and relaxation
Exit through a park side gate, connect to nearby Old Town and Aura River attractions

officialManagement.title: About Kupittaa Park
officialManagement.text:
Kupittaa Park is managed and maintained by the City of Turku. According to the city, it is Finland's oldest urban park, with a history beginning in the 1820s.

Today the park is open to the public free of charge and serves as the core recreational space for Turku residents and an important window for visitors to learn about Finnish history and nature. Park maintenance, playground activities and the outdoor pool season are decided by the city's sports and green-area services; minigolf and the Adventure Park are run by separate operators.

leikkipuisto.metaTitle: Kupittaanpuisto Playgrounds – Kupittaanlahte & Traffic Park, Turku
leikkipuisto.metaDescription: Kupittaanlahte playground, traffic park and Adventure Park in Kupittaa Park, Turku: location, hours, age guidance and family tips.
leikkipuisto.title: Playgrounds & Family Facilities
leikkipuisto.intro: Kupittaa Park is one of Turku's best family destinations because several facilities for different ages sit within the same area. The city-run Kupittaanlahte playground lies along the Kupittaankatu pedestrian avenue near the park's western end. Nearby are the Adventure Park (Seikkailupuisto), run by the children's culture centre Färi, and the traffic park where children practise road rules in miniature.

blocks.title: Kupittaanlahte playground
blocks.content: Address: Kupittaankatu 2, 20520 Turku. The playground sits along the pedestrian avenue from the start of Kupittaankatu, with city-run supervised play activities on weekday mornings. Outside those hours the equipment stays available like elsewhere in the park, and the area is open and free.

blocks.title: Adventure Park (Seikkailupuisto)
blocks.content: Run by the children's culture centre Färi in the southern part of the park on the former gardening-school grounds. Designed for children and families; Färi organises activities year-round for early-education groups and schools. Opening hours vary by season – check Färi's pages.

blocks.title: Traffic park
blocks.content: The traffic park teaches children road rules in a safe environment: miniature routes can be ridden on balance bikes or pedal cars. It has its own website and opening hours; check in advance.

blocks.title: Bird pond and open lawns
blocks.content: The bird pond is a highlight, with a viewing path and benches. Open lawns suit ball games and picnics; the flat path is easy with a pram. A public toilet is in the park.

faq.a: Kupittaanlahte playground is at Kupittaankatu 2, 20520 Turku, along the pedestrian avenue at the start of Kupittaankatu.
Supervised activities on weekday mornings; equipment available during normal park hours.
The playground and park are free. Adventure Park and traffic park may have their own activities; check their pages.
Yes, open year-round; paths can be icy.
Public toilet in the park; lawns and benches suit picnics.

minigolf.metaTitle: Kupittaanpuisto Minigolf – Location, Season & Prices, Turku
minigolf.metaDescription: Kupittaanpuisto Minigolf in Turku: address Kupittaankatu 10, season, pricing and how it differs from the free park.
minigolf.title: Kupittaanpuisto Minigolf
minigolf.intro: Kupittaanpuisto Minigolf is a separate attraction inside the park, run by its own operator. It is not part of the city's free park offering, so the course has its own season, hours and pricing. The course is at Kupittaankatu 10, a short walk from Kupittaanlahte playground.

blocks.title: Location
blocks.content: Kupittaankatu 10, Turku, inside Kupittaa Park, a short walk from the pedestrian avenue. Nearby: playground, Adventure Park, bird pond.

blocks.title: Season & hours
blocks.content: Seasonal: opens in spring, closes in autumn, no rain check. In 2026 the season ran until 27 September, when the course was open on Saturdays and Sundays from 10 to 21. Hours change with the season, so check current times on minigolfturku.fi.

blocks.title: Pricing
blocks.content: Standard playing equipment is included in the green fee; competition balls can be rented for an extra charge. Pricing is split between adults, children and young people, with reduced rates for some groups, and a family package is available. Exact prices change by season, so check the current price list on the operator's site.

blocks.title: On-site services
blocks.content: Italian Minetti ice cream is sold at the course, with lactose-free, gluten-free and vegan options available. Groups of more than ten people are asked to register in advance by email; smaller groups do not need a booking.

faq.a: The course address is Kupittaankatu 10, Turku, inside Kupittaa Park and a short walk from Kupittaanlahte playground.
It is run by the independent operator Kupittaanpuisto Minigolf (Minigolf Turku), not by the City of Turku. Pricing and opening hours are the operator's responsibility.

faq.q: Is minigolf free like the park?
faq.a: No. The park is free, but minigolf has its own player fee that varies by age group. Current prices are listed on the operator's site.
The course is open seasonally from spring to autumn. Opening has recently been concentrated on weekends, but hours vary by season – check them at minigolfturku.fi.
Groups of more than ten people register in advance by email. Smaller parties can simply turn up.

pysakointi.metaTitle: Parking at Kupittaa Park – Driving & Where to Park, Turku
pysakointi.metaDescription: Where to park for Kupittaa Park in Turku: street parking, sports-facility car parks, step-free access and the public-transport option.
pysakointi.title: Parking & Arriving by Car
pysakointi.intro: Kupittaa Park is in the Kupittaa district, where you will find both on-street spaces and car parks serving the Kupittaa sports and event areas. Most visitors find a space quickly on weekdays, but during big events and summer sports days spaces fill early. This guide explains where the spaces are and when it is better to take the bus.

blocks.title: On-street parking
blocks.content: The streets bordering the park – Kupittaankatu among them – offer the largest number of spaces. They are a convenient distance from Kupittaanlahte playground, the bird pond and Adventure Park. Check Turku's current charges, zones and time limits before setting off.

blocks.title: Car parks at the sports facilities
blocks.content: There are car parks at the Kupittaa sports hall, ball games hall, multi-sport court and the field areas. These are the best option if you are heading to sport or an event, since the walk to your destination stays short.

blocks.title: Step-free access
blocks.content: The Kupittaankatu pedestrian avenue running through the park is flat and suits wheelchairs, walkers and prams. The most accessible routes are at the western end of the park, where Kupittaanlahte playground is located.

blocks.title: When to take the bus instead
blocks.content: On event days and warm summer weekends spaces fill up fast. Föli runs several bus routes to the Kupittaa area and the journey from the centre takes only a few minutes – often quicker than searching for a parking space.

faq.q: Is parking at Kupittaa Park free?
faq.a: It depends on the space and Turku's current parking rules. Check current charges and zones in the city's parking information.

faq.q: Where is the parking closest to the playground?
faq.a: The streets along and around Kupittaankatu are closest to Kupittaanlahte playground (Kupittaankatu 2) and the bird pond.

faq.q: How do I reach the park step-free?
faq.a: The Kupittaankatu pedestrian avenue is flat and suits wheelchairs and prams. The step-free route is at the western end of the park.

faq.q: When should I leave the car at home?
faq.a: During a major event or a warm summer weekend. Föli buses are usually the faster option then, and you avoid time spent looking for a space.
Yes. Parking and drop-off are easy along the streets bordering the park, and the walk to the attractions is short.

tapahtumat.metaTitle: Events at Kupittaa Park – Turku Programme & Calendar
tapahtumat.metaDescription: Kupittaa Park's best-known events and where to find this season's programme in Turku.
tapahtumat.title: Events at Kupittaa Park
tapahtumat.intro: Kupittaa Park's wide lawns make it one of Turku's most important outdoor event venues. Large public events have been held here over the years, and in summer especially the area fills with music and gatherings. This site does not maintain its own event calendar; instead it points you to sources that carry the current programme.

blocks.title: New Music Festival
blocks.content: Kupittaa Park has been the main venue of the New Music Festival since 2008. The festival brings several stages and a large audience to the park, so use of the area during the festival differs from normal.

blocks.title: Public gatherings and the Botellón tradition
blocks.content: Since 2009 the park has hosted the Botellón picnic, organised informally through social media without an official organiser. National events have also been held here: the 2012 evangelical festival drew around 12,500 visitors and Yle's summer event in 2025 around 48,500 visitors.

blocks.title: Everyday park life – sport and training
blocks.content: Even without major events Kupittaa Park is in constant use: the multi-sport court, artificial turf pitches, Finnish baseball fields, pétanque courts, basketball court, beach volleyball and fitness stairs shape everyday life. In summer equipment rental at the multi-sport court is free.

blocks.title: Where to find the current programme
blocks.content: We do not publish our own event calendar because we cannot guarantee it stays up to date. Check the current season's programme on the City of Turku and Visit Turku sites as well as each festival's own pages.

faq.q: What events are held at Kupittaa Park?
faq.a: Best known are the New Music Festival, for which the park has been the main venue since 2008, along with various public events and picnics. The programme changes from year to year.

faq.q: Does this site have an event calendar?
faq.a: No. We do not run our own calendar because we cannot guarantee it stays current. Check the programme on the City of Turku, Visit Turku and organisers' own sites.

faq.q: How do I get to large events?
faq.a: Föli buses serve the Kupittaa area on several routes. During major events public transport is usually the best option because parking spaces fill up quickly.
It depends on the event. Some park events are free and others are ticketed. Always check prices on the organiser's own site.

faq.q: Can I visit the park on an event day for other reasons?
faq.a: Usually yes, but some areas may be reserved for the organiser. Check the event details in advance if you are coming to exercise or visit with children.
